title: Regulation of Managed Care and Third Party Administrator Companies
what_it_is: Regulation of Managed Care and Third Party Administrator Companies

sections.label: MOH review of MCCs and TPAs
sections.summary: MOH reviewed MCCs and TPAs, consulting professional and industry bodies, and SMC revised its ethical guidelines effective 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In doing the review, MOH has consulted professional bodies, such as the Singapore Medical Council (SMC), the Singapore Medical Association, the Academy of Medicine Singapore and the College of Family Physicians Singapore, as well as industry associations like the Life Insurance Association (LIA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There is agreement amongst stakeholders that the charging practices must not compromise patient safety and well-being and should not lead to escalation of healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Managed care companies (MCCs) and TPAs provide a wide range of intermediary services, including management of employer medical benefits and claims administration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Those that provide healthcare services directly to patients will be regulated under the Private Hospitals and Medical Clinics Act (PHMCA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To provide clarity on how doctors should engage MCCs and TPAs, the SMC has recently revised its Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (ECEG) to state that doctors must not allow financial arrangements to lead to any compromise in the care of patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Any charges which doctors pay to MCCs or TPAs should be commensurate with the actual administrative work done by these intermediaries in processing the cases, and not based primarily on the fees charged to patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The revised guidelines will take effect from 1 January 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: To enhance transparency of TPA fee arrangements, the revised ECEG indicates that doctors should disclose any such arrangement and referral fees to their patients, if these fees are passed on to the patients.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: MOH is assessing if these disclosure requirements should be further reinforced through our regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: We are also working with LIA and the Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers to ensure that their appointed TPAs do not have any conflict of interest.
